issue.title: Fix silent playback of remuxed takes [Play, record, and re-record audio Audit]
issue.body:
Identified by Roslin while testing #569 on a physical Android device.

**Severity:** High
**Confirmed on:** physical Android devices. The Android emulator plays the same kind of take.

## Summary

#567 records kill-safe ADTS AAC and, on Stop, remuxes it to M4A (`AacRemuxModule`, #233) so Review scrubbing can seek. On device the committed `.m4a` has a duration and plays silence, both in Fluent and in the phone's own player. Skipping the remux and keeping the `.aac` plays with sound, so the recording itself is fine. The emulator accepts the malformed M4A, which is why emulator testing did not show it.

The remux copies each ADTS frame into the MP4 sample, including the ADTS header (`fff1`), and does not write the AAC configuration (`csd-0`) into the container index. The decoder logs `Failed to get extension for extradata parameter` and never opens an audio track. Media volume was not zero.

## Expected

- A take committed after Stop plays with sound on a physical device.
- The committed file stays a seekable M4A, so Review scrubbing still works.
- Kill-safe ADTS capture, background auto-pause, and pause/kill recovery from #567 stay as they are.

## Actual

- New takes recorded after #631 are silent on device.
- The phone player is silent on the same file (`rec_mv8d1dwo_c5185gct.m4a`, Filipenses 4:2).
- The emulator plays.

## Steps to reproduce

1. On a physical Android device, open a verse, record a take, and tap Stop.
2. Tap Play on that take.
3. Open the saved `.m4a` in the phone's player, outside Fluent.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On commit, `AacRemuxModule` strips the ADTS header from each sample and writes the AAC configuration into the M4A index.
- [ ] A new take's first sample does not start with the ADTS sync word (`fff1`).
- [ ] Play on a physical device opens an audio track and produces sound. Waveform scrubbing seeks.
- [ ] The Android emulator still plays the committed take.
- [ ] Pause, kill, relaunch, resume, and stop from #567 still recover the take.
- [ ] Android device QA on a physical device.

Takes already remuxed by the broken converter stay silent. The original `.aac` is deleted after commit. Rewriting those files is out of scope here.

## Related

- Surfaced after #567 (PR #631) switched capture to ADTS
- Remux: #233. Seekable Review playback: #176
- Kill-safe capture spec: #49
- Parent audit: #528
- Found during #569 device testing

comments.body:
## Suggested QA test plan

This is a **suggestion**, based on the steps I used to test this fix locally. It is not a required checklist: feel free to adapt it or add your own checks. It covers the full take recording and playback flow, not only the silent-audio fix.

**Scope of this issue:** #707 fixes only the **silent audio** on new takes. If any step finds a different problem, please report it as a **new bug** instead of reopening this issue.

Run it on a **physical Android device** with the nightly build. Each step lists what should happen; tick the box when it does. If something differs, please note the step number and what you saw.

### A. Record and play

- [ ] 1. Open a verse, record about 10 seconds of continuous speech, and tap Stop. **Expected:** the take appears in the list with a duration of about 0:10.
- [ ] 2. Tap Play. **Expected:** you hear the recording, with sound, from start to end. The timer reaches about 0:10.
- [ ] 3. Let it play to the end. **Expected:** the button goes back to Play and the take does not get stuck.
- [ ] 4. Tap Play again. **Expected:** it plays again from the beginning.
- [ ] 5. Record a short take (about 2 seconds) and a long one (about 60 seconds). **Expected:** both play fully, with sound.

### B. Tapping and dragging on the waveform

- [ ] 6. With the take **stopped**, tap the middle of the waveform. **Expected:** the position jumps to about halfway, and playback does **not** start.
- [ ] 7. Tap Play. **Expected:** playback starts from the middle, not from the beginning.
- [ ] 8. While it is **playing**, tap near the end of the waveform. **Expected:** it jumps there and keeps playing, with no silence.
- [ ] 9. While it is **playing**, tap near the start of the waveform. **Expected:** it jumps back and keeps playing.
- [ ] 10. **Pause** in the middle, then tap another spot on the waveform. **Expected:** the position moves, and it stays paused.
- [ ] 11. After the take finishes playing on its own, tap the middle of the waveform. **Expected:** the position moves, and playback does **not** restart.
- [ ] 12. Drag your finger along the waveform. **Expected:** the position follows your finger, and playback resumes from where you let go.
- [ ] 13. Tap several different spots quickly, one after another. **Expected:** nothing freezes, and the timer matches the spot you tapped.

### C. Pause and resume

- [ ] 14. Play a take, pause at about 0:04, then tap Play. **Expected:** it resumes from 0:04.
- [ ] 15. Pause, switch to the Bible or Resources tab, then come back. **Expected:** the position is still 0:04, and Play resumes from there.

### D. Leaving the app during playback

- [ ] 16. Pause a take in the middle, go to the Android home screen, wait about 10 seconds, and come back. **Expected:** the take is still paused at the same spot, and Play resumes with sound.
- [ ] 17. While a take is **playing**, go to the home screen and come back. **Observation only:** note whether the sound continues or stops while the app is in the background. Today, playback pauses in the background and resumes by itself when you return, with the Pause button showing. When you return, Play and the waveform must still work.
- [ ] 18. Pause in the middle, lock the screen, then unlock it. **Expected:** same as step 16.

### E. Pausing a recording, leaving the app, and recovering a take

- [ ] 19. Record about 5 seconds, tap Pause, record about 5 more seconds, and tap Stop. **Expected:** one take of about 10 seconds. It plays both parts, with sound and no gap.
- [ ] 20. Record about 5 seconds, then go to the home screen **while recording**. **Expected:** the recording pauses by itself. Come back, resume, record about 5 more seconds, and tap Stop. The take is about 10 seconds and plays with sound.
- [ ] 21. Record about 5 seconds and tap Pause. Then **close the app completely** by swiping it away from the recent apps screen. Reopen it and go to the same verse. **Expected:** the paused take is recovered, with the timer showing about 0:05.
- [ ] 22. Continuing from step 21, resume, record about 5 more seconds, and tap Stop. **Expected:** the take is about 10 seconds and plays both parts with sound. The waveform also works on it.
- [ ] 23. Repeat step 21, but this time **discard** the recovered take. **Expected:** it disappears, and the earlier takes are still in the list and still play.
- [ ] 24. Record about 5 seconds and, **without pausing**, close the app completely from the recent apps screen. Reopen it, recover the take, and tap Stop. **Expected:** the take is recovered and plays with sound.

### F. Several takes in one verse

- [ ] 25. With 2 or 3 takes, play take 1. While it plays, tap Play on take 2. **Expected:** take 1 stops and take 2 plays, with sound. Two takes never play at the same time.
- [ ] 26. Select another take and play it once, then tap its waveform. **Expected:** the waveform works on that take. Note: today, a take's waveform only responds after that take has been played, if another take was played before it.
- [ ] 27. Delete a take that is **not** selected. **Expected:** it disappears without asking for confirmation. Then delete the **selected** take. **Expected:** the app asks for confirmation, and the remaining takes still play.
- [ ] 28. In Pericope mode, on a row that combines several verses, tap Play. **Expected:** the parts play one after another, with sound. Tap the middle of the waveform. **Expected:** it jumps to the right verse.

### G. Stability

- [ ] 29. Play a take of about 60 seconds. While it plays, tap many different spots on the waveform quickly (8 to 10 taps). **Expected:** it keeps playing from the last spot. No red error screen appears, and the app does not freeze.
- [ ] 30. With 3 takes, switch Play between them quickly, about 5 times. **Expected:** only one plays at a time, each button shows the right icon, and the app does not freeze or show an error.

### H. Optional: Android emulator

- [ ] 31. If you have an emulator available, repeat steps 1, 2, 6 and 8 there. **Expected:** the take plays with sound, and tapping the waveform works.

**Suggested pass criteria:** sections A, B, C, E, F and G pass on the physical device. Steps 17 and 26 describe current behavior and are for notes only.

Takes recorded **before** this fix will stay silent; that is expected and out of scope. Please test with new recordings.
